Insurance help for DC residents

Whether you are turning 65, already on Medicare and unsure your plan still fits, or shopping for health or life coverage for your family, Honorbrook is here to make it simple. We are an independent agency, which means we work for you and not for any single insurance company. Our job is to help you find the plan that matches your doctors, your prescriptions and your budget.

Our help is free to you. Carriers pay us a commission when we place a policy, and your premium is the same whether you work with us or enroll on your own.

Schedule a Medicare review

Booking opens Luay’s page on PlanEnroll. Create your profile there and ask for your meeting. Having these ready makes the first conversation useful:

  • Your Medicare card, or the dates your Part A and Part B start.
  • The doctors and hospitals you want to keep.
  • A list of your prescriptions and the pharmacy you use.
  • Whether you have Medicaid or get help paying Medicare costs.

When PlanEnroll asks what type of meeting you would like, choose Health. You may be asked to complete a short Scope of Appointment form first. It does not obligate you to enroll. The first open time is at least 24 hours ahead. To talk sooner, call (301) 615-8289 or text (571) 354-0146.

Coverage we help with in Washington, DC

  • Medicare Advantage: all-in-one Part C plans.
  • Medicare Supplement (Medigap): see any doctor who accepts Medicare.
  • Part D drug plans: we compare plans against your medication list.
  • Final expense and life insurance.
  • ACA health plans (under 65), ICHRA and group coverage.
  • Annuities and retirement rollovers.

Products, carriers and rules differ by state. We will confirm what is available at your address before recommending anything.

Free Medicare counseling in Washington, DC, and how we fit in

Washington, DC offers free, unbiased Medicare counseling through the DC State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP), run by the DC Department of Aging and Community Living. It does not sell insurance.

Where Honorbrook adds value is the next step: comparing the specific Medicare Advantage, Medigap and Part D plans offered where you live, checking that your doctors and prescriptions are covered, and helping you enroll and stay on track year after year.

Plan availability varies by county. The Medicare Advantage and drug plans offered at one address are not always offered at the next. We check what is available at your address first, so you only compare plans you can enroll in.

We also help with cancer and critical illness coverage, dental, vision and hearing coverage and hospital indemnity coverage.

Under 65? Health insurance in Washington, DC

Washington, DC runs its own health insurance Marketplace, DC Health Link. Washington, DC has adopted the Affordable Care Act Medicaid expansion, according to KFF’s state tracker (November 2026). Marketplace dates and savings rules change each year, so call us for what applies to you, or read our guide to ACA health insurance. See 2027 Marketplace dates, Medicaid rules and help in Washington, DC.

Your state insurance regulator

The DC Department of Insurance, Securities and Banking regulates insurance in Washington, DC. It can verify an agent’s license and answer consumer questions.

Sources checked November 2026: the DC State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP) page, the CMS Marketplace map for plan year 2027, and KFF’s status of state Medicaid expansion decisions. This page is general information, not insurance advice.

Common questions

Washington, DC FAQ

Do you charge DC residents for help?
No. Our help is free to you. Carriers pay us a commission when we place a policy, and your premium is the same whether you use an agent or enroll on your own.
Do I need to visit an office?
No. Our office is in Tysons, Virginia, and we help DC residents by phone or video call. Office visits are by appointment in Northern Virginia only.
What plans can I get in Washington, DC?
Plan availability varies by county and by carrier. We start with your ZIP code and compare only the plans offered at your address, from the carriers we are appointed with.
Is Honorbrook licensed in Washington, DC?
Yes. Licensed agent Luay Sadqi (NPN 21370662) holds a license for Washington, DC. You can verify any agent’s license with the DC Department of Insurance, Securities and Banking.
